80f3202f3a6ddc68: KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) wants to contest the Melaka election under the Perikatan Nasional (PN) logo.
Its president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin said the party preferred to use the coalition's logo, but would discuss alternatives if necessary.
"If possible, we want to use the PN logo. If not, we will have to sit down again as a team and decide which logo is best for us," he told reporters.
Hamzah said PN had initiated legal action after receiving a notice from the Registrar of Societies (RoS) suspending and subsequently deregistering the coalition on Oct 20.
"When we received the letter from the RoS, we took it to court as quickly as possible.
"That shows we believe the PN logo represents all of us, and that it is our team," he said.
On Oct 22, the High Court granted PN a stay against the RoS action pending the full disposal of its judicial
review, without ruling on the legality of the deregistration.
The ruling allows PN to continue its political activities while the legal challenge is pending.
PN election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor welcomed the decision, saying it would allow the coalition to continue operating pending the judicial review.
Sanusi had earlier said PN was prepared to contest the Melaka polls under the Pas moon logo if it could not use its own.
d37fde17285cf84d: BATU PAHAT: A father was left devastated after one of his four children died and the other three were injured when the car they were travelling in skidded off Jalan Johor Baru-Melaka near Bagan last night.
Noorwandi A Rahim, 41, struggled to hold back his tears as he watched his children's condition before one of them succumbed to his injuries.

Recounting the incident, Noorwandi said he received a call from his younger sibling at about 10pm informing him that the car carrying his children, younger sister and brother-in-law had been involved in an accident.
He said he and his wife, Norfarahin Mohammad, 38, had just arrived home after having dinner together at a shopping mall.
"My wife and I were riding a motorcycle, while our children were in a car driven by my brother-in-law.
"When I arrived at the scene, I saw my children scattered on the road. Putera Muhaimin Qudrat, 16, was lying face down, with his face covered in sand and petrol.

"My wife and I immediately rushed to our other children, Puteri Nur Fairuza Balqis, 15, Putera Khairunas, 11, and Putera Aidin Firdaus, three. My brother-in-law, Nor Azlan Shaharudin, 27, was trapped in the driver's seat.
"I then laid Putera Muhaimin Qudrat down. He responded only once before falling silent.
"The medical team tried to revive him, but my son was pronounced dead," he said when met at the Forensic Department of Hospital Sultanah Nora Ismail (HSNI).
Noorwandi said his youngest child, Putera Aidin Firdaus, was still receiving treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU) at the same hospital.
"Puteri Nur Fairuza Balqis suffered a fractured thigh, chest injuries and slight bleeding in the head, while Putera Khairunas sustained minor injuries and is now in stable condition.
"Putera Aidin Firdaus suffered bleeding in the head, as well as fractures to both arms, legs and a shoulder. He is currently under close observation by the medical team in the ICU.
"My younger sister, Rahmah A Rahim, 26, who is Nor Azlan's wife, is stable and has been warded. She told me that their car was hit from behind before the accident.
"The car then hit a bridge and another vehicle at a workshop before crashing into a coconut tree," he said.

Meanwhile, Batu Pahat district police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani said preliminary investigations found that the car was travelling from Batu Pahat towards Parit Moin, Bagan, when the accident occurred.
He said the driver was believed to have lost control of the vehicle, causing it to skid and crash into a roadside tree.
"All injured victims are still receiving treatment at HSNI. The case is being investigated under the Road Transport Act 1987 for reckless driving causing death," he said.

Commenting on criticism from opposition members of parliament, who claimed he had failed to mediate in the dispute involving MCBA and its personnel, Saifuddin said he accepted the criticism with an open mind.

"Pada masa sama, pendirian ini dapat memperkukuh identiti, akauntabiliti dan keyakinan rakyat terhadap perjuangan PH," katanya dalam kenyataan.
Tegasnya, ancaman terhadap orang Melayu dan Islam bukan berpunca daripada PH atau DAP, sebaliknya amalan politik yang didakwanya diamalkan Umno serta PAS.

Beliau berkata, PH perlu menyatakan dengan jelas ia menolak politik wang Umno dan autokrasi PAS, di samping menjelaskan kepada pengundi, khasnya orang Melayu berhubung keburukan dua amalan politik itu.

"Mereka perlu disedarkan ada politik Melayu yang merupakan pilihan ketiga untuk orang Melayu, yang dibawa oleh Melayu PH, sama ada Amanah, PKR ataupun DAP, yang memperjuangkan tatakelola baik, kecekapan, keberkesanan dan kebajikan.

504cafb8f8c71a1d: PETALING JAYA: Barisan Nasional has rejected Perikatan Nasional's appeal for two more seats under their pact for the Nov 14 Melaka state election.
BN chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the Umno-led coalition is sticking to contesting the lion's share of seats at 21 and allocating seven to PN.
The Umno president added that this was already agreed by PN previously, Bernama reported.

“I have heard about efforts to seek additional seats, but we already have an agreement to allow them to contest the seven seats BN is not contesting. We leave it to PN’s components to distribute those seats among themselves.
“That is the decision for now, and we will stand by what we have mutually agreed upon,” he was quoted as saying.
Previously, PN denied that seat talks with BN had been finalised, after Zahid announced that "PAS and its friends" agreed to contest seven seats under a pact with BN.
PAS deputy president Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man later appealed for PN to be allocated two additional seats.
In the 2021 Melaka polls, BN won 21 seats while Pakatan Harapan secured five and PN two, through Bersatu.
PAS later gained one seat after Rembia assemblyman Jailani Khamis defected from Umno to the Islamic party, before the state's anti-hopping law took effect.

0a7b828c3e2e299a: From S Murugesan
Last night, I used Waze to find a Japanese restaurant in Bukit Jalil. According to Putrajaya, I may have just put national security at risk.
Let me explain how we got here.
First, the government banned civil servants from using Waze. A circular from the Prime Minister's Department cited the app's links to Israel and data security concerns.

Like most Malaysians, I read the news with some amusement and went about my work. It didn't affect me. What the government wants its employees to do is its business, as long as it doesn't affect my life.

To be fair, I can accept the security argument. It's a known fact that data is mined from apps and social media platforms. Information about civil servants in key positions is sensitive, and I can understand the government being cautious.
Ban it for civil servants? Fine. Encourage Malaysians to use TuJu, our very own navigation app? Still fine. Nothing wrong with promoting local services.
Then the prime minister said the government may ban Waze completely for everyone.

A day later, digital minister Gobind Singh Deo said the ban applies only to civil servants on official duty. So which is it? If even the Cabinet cannot agree on how far this goes, ordinary Malaysians can be forgiven for being confused.
Let me be clear. Banning Waze for all of us would be overreach. The government shouldn't take away Malaysians' choices without a very good reason. So far, we haven't been given one.
Where is the evidence?

If the reason is security, kindly explain, in basic terms, how my using Waze to find a restaurant endangers the nation. I am already fully exposed on Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, X and TikTok. What is one more app?
Waze, for its part, has publicly rejected the government's data security claims. If the government has evidence otherwise, please share it. Malaysians can handle the facts.
Why only Waze?
If Waze poses a special threat, tell us why it's being singled out. If the only issue is where the app was founded, then we're on a slippery slope.
Waze has been owned by Google since 2013. My data sits with the same company that runs Google Maps, YouTube and Gmail, and the Android system on most Malaysian phones.
Do we ban those next? Where does it stop?
Is TuJu any safer?
Here is the irony. If spyware like Pegasus, made by Israel's NSO Group, could break into iPhones, how long would it take a determined hacker to break into TuJu?
As an ordinary Malaysian, I would be more worried about my personal information in TuJu than in Waze.
If Waze can misuse my personal data, what is stopping TuJu from doing the same? Who runs TuJu? Who can see my data? Where is it stored?
These are fair questions. Answer them, and TuJu earns our trust. Ignore them, and no ban will fix that.
Let TuJu win on its own

If the real aim is to promote TuJu, the calculation is wrong. People resent being deprived of a choice, especially when they get little in return. Even Gobind told civil servants that if TuJu disappoints, they can use other apps, just not Waze. That is hardly a vote of confidence.

Look, I am happy that we now have our very own navigation app. I will try it. Just let me try it without restricting access to other apps. If, in due time, TuJu turns out to be more user-friendly and caters to my needs, I will use it, without the government pushing it down my throat. Take away my options, and I will resent it.
Competition will make TuJu better. A ban will only build resentment that might show in the next general election.
Build a better map, and Malaysians will find their way to it. No circular required.
S Murugesan is a lawyer and an FMT reader.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
9247456f7dac30a2: I have been breathing the haze, on and off, since I was a child. I was 14 in September 1997, when Sarawak declared a state of emergency after Kuching's air pollutant index (API) reading passed 500, and it later peaked near 800.
I was 30 in June 2013, when Muar's API hit 746. Now it is October 2026, and my son, who has asthma, is stuck indoors. Every trip outside is a risk.
On Oct 9, schools across Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Selangor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan and Johor were shut. Nothing in that timeline is new. What has run out is our patience.
For me, the "Asean Way" on dealing with regional issues has reached its limit, especially when it comes to haze. Asean signed its Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution in 2002.
Indonesia, the last member to ratify it, deposited its instrument in January 2015, 13 years later. The agreement has no meaningful enforcement or dispute-resolution mechanism.
In a resource-constrained world, it means nobody is empowered to act when the sky turns brown. The Covid-19 pandemic showed the same gap, with each government improvising its solutions alone.
Thus, Asean needs a tribunal for environmental harm, built on the logic of the International Criminal Court (ICC), which prosecutes individuals for atrocity crimes.
Vanuatu, Fiji and Samoa proposed adding ecocide to the ICC's statute in September 2024. We should not wait for The Hague.
An Asean Environmental Tribunal would need four powers. Firstly, they must have binding jurisdiction over governments and companies for documented, repeated violations.
Secondly, satellite and concession data must be admitted as evidence and published openly. Thirdly, penalties must include fines, suspension of concessions and personal liability for directors.

Lastly, lenders must be held liable, as they finance the companies behind these fires. A 2019 Forests & Finance report counted about US$19 billion in loans and underwriting to 17 groups linked to Indonesia's fires between 2015 and August 2019.
Malaysian banks were the third-largest source, at about US$2.3 billion, behind China and Indonesia.
I would base the tribunal in Singapore. Its strong institutions and zero tolerance for lax standards, rent-seeking and nepotism make it a credible host. But hosting must come with safeguards.

Singapore suffers from the haze, yet its financial institutions also profit from financing groups linked to the fires. Judges should therefore come from countries not involved in the cases, with strict recusal rules to prevent conflicts of interest.
We are entering an era of climate conflict. We are at war with the planet, and the planet does not negotiate.
Young people across Asean have understood this. They have grown up under the same smoke as their parents, and they will not accept another round of statements of concern.
Asean needs a code of conduct with penalties for breaking it, applied equally to governments and boardrooms alike.
PIAL KHADILLA Managing director — Asean Global Institute For Tomorrow (GIFT)
b89c216d8ba93d95: KUALA LUMPUR: Moto3 rider Hakim Danish Ramli faces a demanding recovery ride in Sunday's Australian Grand Prix after qualifying 23rd at Phillip Island on Saturday.
The AEON Credit-MT Helmets-MSi rider clocked 1 minute 37.169 seconds to finish ninth in the first qualifying session (Q1), missing out on a place in Q2.
Only the top four advanced, with Danish finishing 0.786 seconds behind Indonesia's Veda Pratama, who secured the final qualifying berth before going on to claim pole position.
Danish was 0.908 seconds adrift of Q1 leader Guido Pini of Italy, who topped the session in 1:36.261.
The result leaves the Malaysian on the eighth row alongside Japan's Zen Mitani and Spain's Jesus Rios.
Danish had also struggled for pace on Friday, finishing 25th in practice with a best lap of 1:37.774.
Although he improved that mark by 0.605 seconds in qualifying, it was insufficient to progress.
He will now need to work his way through the field to challenge for points in Sunday's race.
The 19-year-old has already demonstrated his potential this season, claiming his maiden Grand Prix victory at Brno in June.
At the front, Honda Team Asia's Pratama became Indonesia's first Moto3 pole sitter after producing a late lap of 1:35.299.
He edged Spain's Maximo Quiles by just 0.021 seconds, while Australian Joel Kelso completed the front row, a further 0.046 seconds behind.
Danish's teammate Ryusei Yamanaka qualified 17th, leaving both riders with ground to recover on race day.
f123bd77364ac25a: SEREMBAN, Oct 24 — Malaysia stands ready to deliver humanitarian assistance to Yemen, while urging all parties in the protracted conflict in the country to return to the negotiation table and look for a diplomatic solution.

Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Malaysia empathises with the suffering of the Yemeni people who have to endure the effects of the protracted civil war, including famine and hardship in getting basic necessities.

He said the matter was brought up by his counterpart, Yemen’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates, Dr Afrah Abdulaziz Al-Zouba, who shared on the latest developments in the country via a phone call on Thursday.

“Malaysia stands ready to participate in any relief mission or deliver assistance to countries that require it, to the best of our ability,” he told reporters after handing over Deepavali festive contributions at the Rantau community hall here, today.
Mohamad said the conflict must be brought to an end as it brings no benefit to the estimated 22 million affected inhabitants and instead inflicts prolonged suffering.
In light of this, he urged foreign stakeholders to play a constructive role by returning to negotiation table to bring peace and prosperity to the people of Yemen.
He said diplomatic efforts need to be prioritised in order to prevent the conflict from dragging on and undermining regional stability. — Bernama
2be7c7427fe04f81: PUTRAJAYA: Senior civil servants were put through a different kind of leadership test when a shooting sports activity was incorporated into the Advanced Leadership and Management Programme (ALMP) Series 89 No. 4/2026.
The activity was designed to assess participants' ability to plan, manage and coordinate programmes while reinforcing discipline, teamwork and compliance with safety procedures.

National Institute of Public Administration (INTAN) director Dr Mohd Zabri Yusoff said the shooting exercise was more than an introduction to the sport, serving as a practical platform for participants to sharpen their leadership and management skills.
He said the month-long programme emphasised systematic planning, effective coordination and proper implementation to ensure activities achieved their intended objectives.

"Among the aspects we emphasise is how participants plan a programme from the beginning, ensure safety briefings are conducted and carry out activities in accordance with established rules and regulations.

"When they return to their respective agencies, they must ensure that every programme and administrative matter is conducted in compliance with the relevant procedures and regulations," he said at the Shapadu Shooting Range in Precinct 20 today.
Zabri said safety, discipline and adherence to regulations were essential elements in developing effective leadership among senior government officers.
He said the hands-on approach allowed participants to appreciate the importance of meticulous planning, effective coordination and structured implementation in achieving organisational goals.

"The ALMP is a competency development programme that focuses on leadership assessment and strengthening management skills among senior public sector officers, including those holding JUSA C positions.

"The programme brings together officers from various service schemes and professional backgrounds, providing opportunities for them to exchange experiences and establish collaborative networks across government departments and agencies," he said.
He said the professional relationships developed throughout the programme should extend beyond the training period.
He said participants were encouraged to leverage these connections upon returning to their respective agencies to strengthen inter-agency cooperation and collaboration.

"We hope that when participants return to their respective agencies, the relationships established during the programme can be utilised, particularly among senior management, to strengthen cooperation and collaboration," he said.
He added that incorporating shooting sports into the programme reflected INTAN's emphasis on experiential learning in developing public sector leaders.
The approach, he said, reinforced the importance of planning, coordination, procedural compliance and teamwork in ensuring effective public administration.

Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said a specific date for the celebration will be proposed to the Cabinet soon for the government’s approval.
“It will serve as a recognition, a formal acknowledgement that we honour veterans.

“It will also certainly foster closer ties and greater public appreciation for MAF veterans in our country,” he said at the opening ceremony of the 100th National General Assembly of the Malaysian Armed Forces Veterans Association (PVATM) here today.
Also present were Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman, Army Chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman and PVATM president Datuk Sharuddin Omar.

In other developments, Mohamed Khaled said companies awarded major government contracts must provide job opportunities for MAF veterans to ensure they continue to have a place in the economy after completing their service.
He said the Ministry of Defence (Mindef) will monitor the implementation of the initiative to ensure veterans also benefit from these job opportunities.

On Tabung Pahlawan (Warriors’ Fund), he said collections have risen every year, reflecting public appreciation for the contribution of armed forces veterans to safeguarding the nation’s peace and security.
He said collections increased from RM1.3 million in 2023-2024 to RM2.19 million in 2024-2025 and RM3.35 million in 2025-2026.
He added that collections for 2026-2027 have so far reached RM4.35 million, against a target of RM5 million. — Bernama
7d369ca8b550f891: KUALA LUMPUR: Police will summon a podcaster to assist in an investigation into claims made on a podcast about drug dealing near the Sentul police headquarters.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said statements had so far been recorded from four people.

The case is being investigated under Section 505 of the Penal Code for statements conducing to public mischief and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act for misuse of network facilities.
The offences are punishable by jail terms and a fine.
"We will refer the case to the prosecution as soon as possible," he said on the sidelines of a Taman Angkat Amanita programme.
Fadil said people sharing their experiences on podcasts must do so responsibly to avoid misleading the public or disrupting public order.
"Give us time to complete our investigation," he said.
On Oct 20, Sentul police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said police would record a statement from a former journalist who appeared as a guest on the podcast.
This followed a police report over claims made on the podcast about an incident in 2016.
The former journalist claimed he had monitored drug dealing at a disused house of worship near a police station in Sentul.

dcacec931418d126: KUALA LUMPUR: Businessman Datuk Seri Farhash Wafa Salvador Rizal Mubarak has initiated legal proceedings against former economy minister Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli over allegedly defamatory statements made about him in a podcast.

Farhash's lawyer, Datuk Seri Rajan Navaratnam, said the writ and statement of claim were filed on Oct 23, with the court documents in the process of being served on Rafizi in accordance with the relevant procedures.

In a statement issued on behalf of his client, Rajan said the legal action stemmed from a podcast titled "Dari Umno ke PKR: Zetrix – Kerajaan Bertukar, Kroni Berpindah? | YBM #68", published on Rafizi's YouTube channel on Oct 16.

The podcast, which runs for about three hours and 14 minutes, contains statements concerning Farhash's alleged business interests, corporate relationships, purported links to political figures, and allegations relating to cronyism and government contract procurement.
Rajan said this was the second legal action initiated by Farhash against Rafizi.
"Our client maintains that the repeated publication of defamatory statements concerning him is tainted with malicious intent and has the effect of tarnishing his reputation.
"Therefore, our client considers it necessary to take legal action against Datuk Seri Mohd Rafizi Ramli," he said.
He said Farhash took the allegations seriously and believed such matters should be addressed through the proper legal process and determined based on the evidence and applicable law.
"As solicitors for our client, we do not intend to litigate this matter through the media or engage in public exchanges concerning the merits of the case.
"Ultimately, our client leaves the matter to the court to decide," he said.
33a125d9064993b8: PUTRAJAYA: Foreigners are resorting to marrying elderly Malaysian women, including widows and single mothers, to register vehicles in their spouses' names in a bid to circumvent stricter enforcement against foreign drivers.

Road Transport Department (RTD) senior enforcement director Datuk Muhammad Kifli Ma Hassan said investigations had revealed that some foreigners were targeting Malaysian women aged 60 and above, promising to marry them in exchange for allowing their names to be used for vehicle registration.
He said it was a new modus operandi adopted by foreign drivers in response to intensified enforcement operations since July.
"These foreigners are targeting women aged 60 and above, particularly single mothers, widows and unmarried women.
"They make sweet promises of marriage to persuade these women to allow their names to be used for vehicle registration.

"Some even go through with the marriage solely for the purpose of using their spouses' names," he told reporters at the Advanced Leadership and Management Programme (ALMP) Series 89 No. 4/2026 at the Shapadu Shooting Range in Precinct 20 today.
Kifli described the tactic as dangerous, warning Malaysians against allowing their personal details to be exploited for vehicle ownership.
He said the department had stepped up enforcement under Op Pewa following instructions from RTD director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli in July.
Under the stricter enforcement measures, both foreign drivers and vehicle owners would face action if offences were detected.
"We will issue summonses to both the driver and the vehicle owner, while the vehicles involved will be seized.
"We will not offer compounds, meaning these cases will be brought to court.
"This is to demonstrate how seriously we view these offences, as action will be taken against both the driver and the owner," he said.
He said RTD had issued a total of 523,035 summons notices under Op Pewa between 2024 and Oct 15 this year.
Of the total, 183,300 notices were issued in 2024, followed by 191,676 last year and 148,059 so far this year.
He advised Malaysians against renting out their vehicles or allowing them to be used by foreigners who were not legally permitted to drive.
"We need the cooperation of all Malaysians to ensure that foreign drivers do not continue operating freely on our roads.
"If Malaysians refuse to allow their vehicles to be used by these foreigners, they will not be able to drive on our roads," he said.
d18b2da89dfeb3b9: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ordered a thorough, transparent and uncompromising investigation into the death of Noorizwan Zulkefly in police custody.

In a Facebook post today, Anwar said he had contacted Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail to obtain further information on the case and ensure that updates on the investigation were conveyed to the deceased’s family.
He said he understood the family’s grief and anxiety as they awaited answers regarding Noorizwan’s death.

“I acknowledge the presence of the late Noorizwan’s family to submit an appeal letter to me today. I am deeply saddened by his passing and understand the family’s grief and anxiety as they await answers,” he said.
Anwar, who was scheduled to attend several programmes in Melaka today, said he had delegated his officers to receive the appeal letter and listen to the concerns raised by the family.
Media reports previously said police were still awaiting the full report from the Chemistry Department and the pathology findings to determine the actual cause of the man’s death on Oct 1.
Noorizwan was detained by the Cheras District Police Headquarters to assist in investigations under Section 39A(1) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, as well as Sections 457 and 379 of the Penal Code.
He was subsequently referred to Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM) on Sept 30 for treatment and was pronounced dead at 1.52 am the following day. — Bernama
33383b0005acc840: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have detained two foreigners in connection with the discovery of a dead baby girl in a rubbish bin in Abdullah Hukum, Bangsar, yesterday.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the suspects, a 23-year-old man and a 31-year-old woman, were arrested in Brickfields following investigations and tip-offs from the public.
"We believe they are linked to this case, and investigations are ongoing.

"We also appreciate the information provided by the public, which helped police track them down," he said at a press conference after the Wangsa Maju police headquarters Amanita Adoptive Park programme at PPR Laksamana, Jalan Peel, here today.
Asked whether the suspects were married, Fadil said it was still under investigation.
He said the baby was believed to have been around seven months into the pregnancy when Alam Flora workers found her body at a waste disposal area near Abdullah Hukum.
The case is being investigated under Section 318 of the Penal Code.
Brickfields district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hoo Chang Hook said yesterday that police received a report of the discovery at 10.43am.
The body was found in a rubbish bin in an apartment complex before being sent to the Kuala Lumpur Hospital Forensic Unit for a post-mortem.
c8c8acda8cf0cd7a: About 200 firefighters deployed to tackle the blaze at former Nazi retreat in a remote part of southern Germany German police said Saturday they had detained a suspect after a fire at Adolf Hitler’s former mountain retreat, known as the Eagle’s Nest, in the state of Bavaria. About 200 firefighters were deployed to tackle the blaze at the Nazi dictator’s remote and difficult-to-access Kehlsteinhaus residence, on the peak of Obersalzberg in southern Germany. 440b1e58fb362c9f: PETALING JAYA: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has contacted Inspector-General of Police Khalid Ismail to obtain further information on the custodial death of the late Noorizwan Zulkefly, 42.
Anwar said he was also grieved by Noorizwan's death on Oct 1 and understood the sadness and unease shared by the family of the deceased.

"I have stressed (to Khalid) that the investigation should be conducted thoroughly, transparently, and without compromise, and that its developments should be communicated to the family," he said in a post on X.

Earlier today, Noorizwan's family submitted a letter to Anwar seeking the prime minister's assurance that the detainee's death would be investigated transparently and that the family would be updated regularly.
Anwar's aide received the letter on his behalf.

"I am not asking the prime minister to determine who is guilty or to impose a sentence. I only ask that justice be served firmly, freely, and without unreasonable delays," Noorizwan's younger brother, Nooranis Zulkefly, said in the letter.
He also urged Anwar to order the authorities to stop "harassing" the family's lawyers as they seek information on the detainee's death.
He said the lawyers should be able to carry out their professional duties for the family without the authorities intimidating them.

This comes after lawyers Latheefa Koya, N Surendran and Dina Zamri were questioned by federal police for visiting Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz UKM’s (HUKM) pathology unit to obtain clarification on Noorizwan’s autopsy report and to view photographs of his injuries.
Noorizwan was arrested on Sept 20 and held at the Cheras police headquarters for 11 days before being taken to HUKM on Sept 30. He was pronounced dead on Oct 1.
The family previously rejected the police's insistence that Noorizwan's arrest and detention were conducted in accordance with SOPs.
Earlier today, Bukit Aman said Noorizwan suffered several external injuries but did not suffer any internal bleeding. Nonetheless, the cause of death is pending laboratory analysis.
323afe83d1cfb6b6: WASHINGTON, Oct 24 — Iran has “substantially increased” its efforts to target Americans in the Middle East and beyond, US national intelligence chief Jay Clayton warned on Friday.
The warning comes after Washington ordered non-essential US embassy staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia this week, following increasing attacks from Yemen’s Houthis.
The kingdom has come under near-daily attacks this month from the Iran-backed group, including a strike on Riyadh’s international airport that was the kingdom’s deadliest in years.
“We have received intelligence that Iran has substantially increased efforts to target US personnel,” Clayton said in a memo sent to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, according to a US official.
“The lethal plotting efforts by the Iranians against US citizens have reached advanced stages in both the Middle East and certain other countries,” said the memo, which was first reported by Axios.
Washington previously ordered non-essential staff to leave the Gulf ahead of the start of its war against Iran and again in July before US President Donald Trump called off a new wave of strikes.
The US official said: “When it comes to our staffing at embassies, we constantly evaluate new information about the security environment.”
“The threat of Houthi attacks and of Iranian terror plots targeting US officials are informing our decisions,” the official added.
Trump suggested on Friday that the US might launch renewed military operations against Iran.
“We may do another little Epic Fury” Trump said, referring to the US name for its attacks on Iran. He did not give any indication on timing.
The conflict began in late February with US-Israeli attacks on Iran, killing the country’s supreme leader, along with senior military commanders. — AFP
3a6a609851bbcaaa: KULAI, Oct 24 — The National Registration Department (JPN) has issued 275,785 new-generation MyKad nationwide since its launch on Sept 17 until Oct 20, with Johor recording the highest number at 31,392 cards.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the figures reflected a positive response from the public to the new-generation MyKad, which comes with enhanced security features.
He said the new-generation MyKad incorporates 53 security features, compared with 23 in the previous version, including a transparent window, QR code, ultraviolet features, hologram and microtext.
The enhancements were introduced to ensure the identity card’s security features remained relevant to technological advancements, following about 12 years of use of the previous MyKad generation.
“JPN has taken steps to further upgrade the security features. That is why we call it the new-generation MyKad,” he said.

“Johor recorded the highest number, with 31,392 cards issued, followed by Kuala Lumpur with 29,601, Selangor (26,736), Sarawak (25,642) and Sabah (22,523),” he told a press conference after officiating the 78th National Registration Day celebration and the launch of the Madani Adopted Village and Madani Adopted School initiatives at the Kampung Melayu Sedenak Multipurpose Hall here today.
Saifuddin Nasution said the public need not rush to replace their MyKad, as JPN had assured that the supply of cards was sufficient to meet demand.

He said about 24 million existing MyKads were currently in circulation, while JPN received an average of 200,000 applications a month for various purposes, including new identity cards, replacements for damaged cards and MyKad issuance to those turning 18.

He said possession of a MyKad was becoming increasingly important due to various government initiatives requiring its use, including purchases of petrol and cooking oil, as well as the redemption of Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA).

“We do not have any projections. We will continue as usual and serve the public. What matters is ensuring that the card supply is sufficient to meet demand from those who choose to switch to the new-generation MyKad,” he said. — Bernama
056efe5b299eca26: PETALING JAYA: Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim menghubungi Ketua Polis Negara Khalid Ismail bagi mendapatkan maklumat lanjut berhubung kematian Noorizwan Zulkefly dalam tahanan awal bulan ini, sambil menegaskan siasatan perlu dijalankan menyeluruh, telus dan tanpa kompromi.
Anwar turut menegaskan perkembangan siasatan dimaklumkan kepada keluarga mangsa.
Beliau berkata, pihaknya mengambil maklum kehadiran keluarga Noorizwan untuk menyerahkan surat rayuan kepadanya hari ini.

“Saya mengambil maklum kehadiran keluarga Allahyarham Noorizwan Zulkefly untuk menyerahkan surat rayuan kepada saya hari ini, dan amat berdukacita atas pemergian Allahyarham serta memahami kesedihan dan keresahan keluarga yang menantikan jawapan.

“Saya dijadualkan menghadiri beberapa rencana di Melaka hari ini dan telah mewakilkan pegawai saya untuk menerima surat tersebut serta mendengar sendiri perkara yang dibangkitkan keluarga,” katanya dalam kenyataan.

Terdahulu, keluarga Noorizwan bersama peguam hadir ke kediaman perdana menteri bagi menyerahkan memorandum dan menggesa campur tangan kerajaan berhubung kematian mangsa ketika dalam tahanan di IPD Cheras.
Noorizwan ditangkap pada 20 Sept lalu dan ditahan di IPD Cheras selama 11 hari tanpa pengetahuan keluarganya sebelum dibawa ke Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz UKM pada 30 Sept.
Dia disahkan meninggal dunia pada 1 Okt.
Keluarganya menolak dakwaan ketua polis Kuala Lumpur bahawa tangkapan dan penahanan dijalankan mengikut SOP.

Pada 12 Okt, seorang pakar patologi forensik kanan di hospital berkenaan dilaporkan mengesahkan kepada keluarga dan pasukan peguam mereka punca kematian Noorizwan disebabkan trauma daya tumpul pada bahagian kepala.
Hari ini, Bukit Aman memaklumkan berdasarkan hasil bedah siasat dijalankan mendapati tiada sebarang kecederaan organ dalaman, namun terdapat beberapa kecederaan pada bahagian luaran.
“Punca kematian telah dinyatakan sebagai menunggu keputusan analisis makmal,” kata Pengarah Jabatan Integriti dan Pematuhan Standard, Aida Abdul Hamid dalam kenyataan.
9c0d702834645d08: PETALING JAYA: The RM43 million anti-drone systems procured from Japan will be stationed in several strategic locations in Malaysia, including Labuan and Sepanggar in Sabah.

Defence minister Khaled Nordin said the counter-unmanned aircraft systems (C-UAS) supplied under an official security assistance programme by Japan is aimed at bolstering Malaysia's preparedness for drone attacks, Berita Harian reported.
"We are facing a very different geopolitical situation and are located in a region with distinct challenges. As I've often stressed, we are a maritime nation.
"As much as we defend our land, we must also protect our entire maritime domain. We must control our waters, including in the Straits of Melaka and the South China Sea," he was quoted as saying.

"We are also well aware that the South China Sea includes areas disputed by China, Vietnam and the Philippines. Therefore, we must ensure our defence capabilities to maintain control over our maritime domains."
Japan will provide the Malaysian navy with the C-UAS under a RM43 million deal signed by Khaled and Japan's foreign minister, Toshimitsu Motegi, on Oct 20.

This marks the first time that Japan is supplying the C-UAS to Malaysia under its official security assistance programme. Seen as a strategic partner of Japan's, Malaysia has been a recipient of this security assistance since 2023.
f6cdd0df83ad95e7: REMBAU: Malaysia is prepared to provide any form of assistance to Indonesia in tackling transboundary haze, including seeking support from Gulf countries if necessary.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Malaysia understood the difficulties faced by Indonesia in managing extensive forest fires in areas far from its borders.
He said he would contact his Indonesian counterpart, Arrmanatha Christiawan Nasir, soon to discuss the assistance required.

"I also agreed with United Arab Emirates Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah Zayed Al Nahyan yesterday when he said that if assistance was needed, he was prepared to work with other countries to provide it.

"If Indonesia requires assistance, I will raise the matter with my counterparts in the Gulf countries to provide whatever help is needed," he told reporters after presenting Deepavali contributions to recipients in the Rantau state constituency at Dewan Orang Ramai Rantau here today.
Mohamad said Malaysia could not remain silent as forest fires in Indonesia also affected neighbouring countries, but any assistance operation would need to take safety considerations into account.
The Rembau member of Parliament said firefighting operations faced major challenges because the fires were located deep in remote areas, while thick haze had also reduced visibility.
He said developed countries such as Canada and the United States had also experienced forest fires, including those in Los Angeles that claimed many lives.

"It is easy for us to talk about it here, but imagine if the fires were 1,000km or even 500km from residential areas. There would be no other option but to use aircraft. However, aircraft would also be unable to carry out firefighting operations because of limited visibility," he said.

Meanwhile, Mohamad said Malaysia was prepared to provide humanitarian assistance to Yemen following discussions with Yemen's Foreign Affairs and Expatriates Minister, Dr Afrah Abdulaziz Al-Zouba, yesterday.

He also expressed hope that the civil war in Yemen could be brought to an end, saying the conflict had brought no benefits to the country's people and had left 22 million people bearing its consequences, including many facing starvation.
"Malaysia has expressed its sympathy and is prepared to participate in any relief mission or provide assistance.
"We also call on the parties with interests in the conflict from outside Yemen to come to the negotiating table so that the Yemeni people can enjoy a peaceful and prosperous life," he said.
a709014d8cb9d474: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Bursa Malaysia is likely to trend upwards next week, with the benchmark index expected to trade within the 1,600-1,620 range amid a recovery in investors’ risk appetite, said an analyst.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng expects bargain hunting to intensify as investors take advantage of increasingly attractive valuations.
However, elevated crude oil prices, geopolitical uncertainties and persistent foreign selling could trigger intermittent volatility, he added.

“Overall, we anticipate the FBM KLCI to trade within the 1,600-1,620 range next week, with a mildly positive bias supported by selective accumulation of fundamentally sound stocks,” Thong told Bernama.
He added that Malaysia’s resilient economic fundamentals and relatively contained inflation should continue to underpin corporate earnings prospects.
Meanwhile, Thong said the recent correction has brought selected blue chip stocks to more attractive valuations, particularly within the banking, plantation and utilities sectors.

For the week just ended, the local bourse traded mostly lower, in tandem with most regional markets, tracking Wall Street performance due to concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) investment sustainability
On a Friday-to-Friday basis, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 3.80 points to 1,611.56 from 1,607.76 a week earlier.
On the index board, the FBM Emas Index added 1.18 points to 11,993.45, the FBM Top 100 Index increased 10.84 points to 11,797.61, and the FBM Emas Shariah Index garnered 23.70 points to 11,943.57.
The FBM ACE Index dipped 84.93 points to 5,346.14 and the FBM Mid 70 Index decreased 55.61 points to 17,170.33.

By sector, the Energy Index advanced 13.67 points to 834.67, the Plantation Index gained 44.60 points to 8,677.48, and the Industrial Products and Services Index climbed 2.61 points to 175.4. The Financial Services Index tumbled 97.50 points to 18,654.32.

df98c5c2c045fc99: Established under the Franco dictatorship, the lunchtime ritual is in decline but all is not lost A little before lunchtime each working day across Spain, evidence of one of the lingering, if less notorious, legacies of the Franco dictatorship is carefully traced in chalk, marker pen and printer ink. 343ea5f30a1275cc: Turning boarded-up shops into community spaces is a bigger and more complex task than just adding funding Most levelling up projects still unfinished years after funding allocated “It is nice to see something happening for once,” says Jack Vincent, a Grimsby resident, as he considers a wave of change finally arriving in a town that had become a byword for deprivation. 10629099d2e40e38: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The ringgit is expected to trade within a narrow range of RM4.07 to RM4.08 against the US dollar next week as investors monitor the outcome of the US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting scheduled for October 27-28.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said investors will also look for clues on the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy direction from the FOMC statement and subsequent press conference, with markets expecting the Fed funds rate to remain unchanged at 3.75 to 4.00 per cent.

“Essentially, the Fed’s assessment of inflation and the prevailing market conditions surrounding artificial intelligence investments and equity valuations will be critical elements in shaping market confidence.
“More importantly, it is whether there will be any change in tone regarding the current monetary policy stance and the outlook for current and future inflation rates,” he told Bernama.
Hence, he said the US dollar-ringgit pair is expected to trade within a narrow range.
Meanwhile, on a Friday-to-Friday basis, the ringgit eased against the greenback to 4.0835/0875 from 4.0795/0835 a week earlier.
The local currency traded mostly lower against a basket of other major currencies during the week.

It inched down vis-a-vis the Japanese yen to 2.6076/6103 from 2.5831/5895 on the previous Friday and depreciated against the British pound to 5.4633/4687 from 5.4396/4449, but it gained versus the euro to 4.5735/5780 from 4.5911/5956 a week earlier.
The ringgit traded mostly higher against Asean currencies.

It climbed vis-a-vis the Thai baht to 12.0985/1154 from 12.2101/2268 a week earlier, inched up against the Indonesian rupiah to 225.8/226.1 from 226.3/226.6 and went up against the Philippine peso to 6.42/6.43 from 6.48/6.49
The local note, however, declined versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1952/1986 from 3.1889/1922 at the end of last week. — Bernama
4f17cb65833fcfb8: KUCHING: Pas will likely contest three state seats in the coming Sarawak election, says the Islamist party's state chief, Mohammad Arifiriazul Paijo.
He said the party was eyeing Semariang, Sebuyau and Beting Maro, although the final decision rested with the Pas central leadership.
He said Sarawak Pas had proposed contesting the three seats and that its election machinery in the areas was ready.
Arifiriazul said the party was also considering contesting another seat in northern Sarawak, either within the Bintulu or Sibuti parliamentary constituency.
However, he said Pas was not ready to disclose which seat it was considering.
Arifiriazul said they have also shortlisted candidates for the three seats.
On whether Pas would contest on its own or with other parties, he said discussions with several political partners were still ongoing and had yet to be finalised.
However, he said the outcome of those talks would not affect Pas' decision to contest the three seats, whether as part of a coalition or on its own.
Asked whether Pas could become part of the state government if it won any seats, he said the matter would only be decided when the time came.
"We are contesting this election to serve the local people and provide the best possible service to communities in the areas we contest.
Arifiriazul said Pas' victory in Sabah in the recent state election had also boosted morale among its 8,000 members in Sarawak.
Last night, Perikatan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the coalition, which Pas leads, had yet to decide on contesting in the Sarawak election.
7f45214c9193d736: PHILLIP ISLAND (Australia): Marc Marquez stormed home first from pole in the Australian MotoGP sprint race on Saturday to seize control of the world championship from Jorge Martin who crashed out challenging him for the lead.
The reigning seven-time world champion, who dominated qualifying, had too much power in his Ducati to surge to the chequered flag ahead of his brother Alex in the 13-lap contest.
Victory put him 10 points clear of fellow Spaniard Martin in the standings ahead of the final MotoGP ever around the waterfront Phillip Island circuit on Sunday.
Martin, who started from fourth under dark clouds but with the rain staying away, took the lead on lap three in a ding-dong battle with his rival.
But he lost control on lap eight while challenging for the lead once again to put a massive dent in his championship ambitions.
"It was a tight battle," said Marquez. "Of course, I gave everything. I was aggressive, and he (Martin) was faster than me.
"But just I tried to defend in the best way possible. Both of us we are riding to the limit. Both of us, we deserve the victory because we are pushing a lot.
"But, you know, racing is like it is."
His brother Alex, who started second, filled an all-Ducati podium with Fabio Di Giannantonio.
Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi, who won the MotoGP last week in Indonesia, was fourth to remain third in the standings, 50 points behind Marquez.
Pedro Acosta (KTM) came fifth and Ai Ogura (Aprilia) sixth.
Marc Marquez held the line to be first at the opening corner with Martin up to second with Johann Zarco third and it stayed that way at the end of lap one.
Martin was pressing hard and he took the lead on lap three as the race became a dogfight between the two championship leaders as they pulled clear of the field.
A big mistake from Martin running wide on lap five opened the door again for Marquez, with the lead changing hands several times as they battled for supremacy.
But Martin pushed too much and sensationally lost control on lap eight, skidding out to end his race.
Phillip Island has been a staple on the calendar since 1997 but the Australian race is moving next year to a street circuit in Adelaide. - AFP
84a4415ba3b078ba: SHAH ALAM, Oct 24 — Edaran Otomobil Nasional Bhd (EON) has strengthened its after-sales services for customers with the launch of its first vehicle body and paint repair hub in Glenmarie here.

Spanning 41,508 square feet, the centre is equipped with 39 work bays, three paint-mixing rooms and four spray booths to meet the repair and restoration needs of various vehicle brands under EON, including Proton, Mitsubishi, Audi and smart electric vehicles. 1578cbfe83b7e133: GEORGE TOWN: Berita Harian (BH) and Harian Metro (HM) have been recognised by Dewan Bahasa dan Pustaka (DBP) for their contributions to promoting and strengthening the use of Bahasa Melayu.
Both publications received the Hadiah Citra Bahasa Sahabat DBP 2026 at the launch of the 2026 National Language Month at Padang Kota here.
BH group editor Zulkifli Jalil and HM group editor Husain Jahit received the awards.

The Hadiah Citra Bahasa Sahabat DBP recognises organisations from the public and private sectors, as well as non-governmental organisations, for their contributions and commitment to promoting the national language.
Recipients receive a certificate of appreciation and RM5,000 in collaboration funding to organise literary bazaar activities.
The ceremony also saw the presentation of the Hadiah Citra Bahasa 2026, which recognises high achievement in Bahasa Melayu proficiency assessments. Recipients received RM3,000.

The Anugerah Ikon Bahasa 2026 was presented to lyricist and writer Datuk Habsah Hassan, professional emcee Terence Joseph Dass and Penang Mufti Associate Professor Datuk Dr Mohd Suki Othman for their contributions to upholding the national language.
Each recipient received RM2,000, a certificate of appreciation and books published by DBP.
The awards were presented by Education Ministry deputy director-general (Professional Development Sector) Datuk Amzan Abd Malek.
Husain said HM would continue to champion Bahasa Melayu at both national and international levels.
He said the recognition reflected the newspaper's continued commitment to promoting the national language through its media platforms and initiatives.
"We are proud to receive this award, as it shows that HM continues to be recognised," he said.
Husain said HM had recently organised a pantun competition in collaboration with DBP and DRB-HICOM to promote the Malay language and preserve its literary heritage.
He said pantun, a traditional Malay poetic form, remained an important part of Bahasa Melayu and a valuable medium for nurturing public appreciation of the language.
Meanwhile, Zulkifli said young people should use Bahasa Melayu wisely and preserve its integrity as a reflection of their identity.
He said the tendency to modify the language on social media to suit individual preferences should not come at the expense of its proper use.
"If we look at social media, much of our language has been modified to suit their tastes. However, we should preserve the national language because it reflects our identity," he said.
Zulkifli also highlighted the role of newspapers in helping young people improve their language proficiency, particularly in grammar and writing.
He encouraged students to read newspapers, including BH, the New Straits Times (NST) and other publications circulated in schools.
"Newspapers use language that is proper and somewhat academic. I hope students will return to reading newspapers, especially to learn from the grammar used," he said.
He said regular exposure to well-written news articles could help students better understand Bahasa Melayu and use it appropriately in everyday communication.

d297228511833aa9: PETALING JAYA: Sistem pemintas pesawat tanpa pemandu (C-UAS) atau antidron yang bakal diterima daripada Jepun akan ditempatkan di beberapa lokasi strategik, termasuk Sepanggar dan Labuan.
Menteri Pertahanan, Khaled Nordin, berkata sistem yang dibekalkan menerusi program Bantuan Keselamatan Rasmi Jepun itu bertujuan memperkukuhkan keupayaan negara berdepan ancaman serangan dron.
"Seperti yang sering saya tegaskan, kita adalah negara maritim. Kita mempertahankan wilayah daratan, tetapi pada masa sama mesti melindungi keseluruhan domain maritim negara.
"Kita juga sedia maklum Laut China Selatan adalah kawasan bertindih tuntutan wilayah, terutama membabitkan China, Vietnam dan Filipina.

"Justeru, kita mesti memastikan keupayaan untuk mengekalkan kawalan ke atas domain maritim kita," katanya menurut Berita Harian selepas merasmikan Perhimpunan Agung Tahunan Ke-100 Persatuan Veteran Angkatan Tentera Malaysia di Kuala Lumpur.

Jepun akan membekalkan sebuah sistem C-UAS bernilai 1.65 bilion yen atau kira-kira RM43 juta kepada Tentera Laut Diraja Malaysia (TLDM) menerusi program Bantuan Keselamatan Rasmi bagi tahun fiskal 2026, yang dimeterai Khaled bersama Menteri Luar Jepun, Toshimitsu Motegi di Tokyo pada 20 Okt lalu.

Menurut Kementerian Luar Jepun, projek itu dijangka meningkatkan keupayaan keselamatan TLDM, termasuk dari segi pemantauan dan pengawasan, yang juga projek pertama negara itu membekalkan sistem C-UAS menerusi kerangka program berkenaan.
Khaled berkata, Malaysia dan Jepun mempunyai hubungan erat dua hala sejak sekian lama, dengan kerjasama pertahanan semakin kukuh dalam beberapa tahun ini susulan perubahan dasar pertahanan Tokyo.
Beliau berharap program Bantuan Keselamatan Rasmi Jepun itu akan berterusan kerana ia banyak membantu Malaysia dalam membangunkan keupayaan pertahanan negara.

"Malaysia turut memohon bantuan pada masa depan memberi tumpuan kepada keutamaan strategik, termasuk meningkatkan keupayaan mempertahankan domain maritim di tengah-tengah cabaran geopolitik dan tuntutan bertindih di Laut China Selatan.
"Kesiapsiagaan pertahanan Malaysia bukan sahaja bergantung kepada aset tentera dan anggotanya, tetapi juga rakan kerjasama dipercayai yang bersedia membantu meningkatkan keupayaan negara."

Malaysia antara penerima awal program itu sejak 2023. Jepun menyifatkan Malaysia sebagai rakan strategik di laluan maritim penting antara Lautan Hindi dengan Asia Timur, selain berdepan Selat Melaka dan bahagian selatan Laut China Selatan.

5a866d923ec536ea: PETALING JAYA: Amanah communications director Khalid Samad has urged Pakatan Harapan to go solo in the upcoming Melaka polls and the next general election (GE16), particularly to take on Umno and PAS.

799db4e77934ba71: KUALA LUMPUR: Growing up with poor vision, Wong Kar Gee spent years competing against able-bodied athletes before discovering para-sports,
Now after winning an Asian Para Games gold in Nagoya, Japan on Wednesday. the 35-year-old Sabahan believes he is on course for a Paralympic medal.

Kar Gee triumphed in the men's long jump T12 after leaping 6.74 metres. He posted his winning distance on his opening attempt, before clearing 6.60m, 6.47m, 6.36m, 6.39m, and 6.40m on his remaining jumps.
Uzbekistan's Sevinchbek Khusanov finished second (6.54m) while Japan's Daiki Ishiyama was third (6.48m).
For Kar Gee, it was an improvement as he claimed silver in the same event at the 2018 Jakarta edition. He missed the last Games, in 2022 in Hangzhou due to injury.
"I'm glad to finally compete in the Asian Para Games again and win gold," he said.

Kar Gee's journey into para-sports began only in 2017. "I was studying in a normal school and competing with able-bodied athletes until 2016. It was only in 2017 that I learnt about para-sports and decided to make the move," he said.
Diagnosed with Stargardt disease at the age of eight, Kar Gee had impaired vision but said his family never treated him differently.
"I basically grew up like any normal child. My parents and family never treated me differently," he said.
However, Kar Gee's poor eyesight posed challenges when he pursued tertiary studies in Australia, as he struggled to read textbooks.
"I had problems reading books. I told my mother, and she asked me to return home and focus on the family business," he said.
Back in Sabah, Kar Gee trains at least once a day while running a farm that includes poultry, prawns and hydroponics.
The entrepreneur credits his family for enabling him to balance his sporting ambitions, business responsibilities and life with his wife and one-year-old daughter, Charlotte.
"I can focus on my sports, work, manage my farm, as well as my family because I'm blessed with family members who can handle things without me. It gives me the space to do all these things," he said.
For now, there is a gold medal to celebrate. Kar Gee said he would mark his Nagoya triumph with a family dinner alongside relatives and friends when he returns home.

Kar Gee came close to winning a Paralympic medal before. He finished fourth in the long jump T12 at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, missing the podium by just three centimetres with a mark of 6.85m behind Argentina's Fernando Vazquez who took bronze (6.88m).
He feels his latest success will give him the momentum to challenge for a medal at the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics.
"I believe this gold medal can bring me closer to the podium at the 2028 Los Angeles Paralympics. I believe I will be able to improve my jumps for LA 2028," said Kar Gee.
With the support of the National Sports Council, the long jumper hopes to make the leap to the Paralympic podium.

51f3c67493c2fb6b: KULAI: The National Registration Department (JPN) has issued 275,785 new-generation MyKad nationwide since its launch on Sept 17 until Oct 20, with Johor recording the highest number at 31,392 cards.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the figures reflected a positive response from the public to the new-generation MyKad, which comes with enhanced security features.

He said the new-generation MyKad incorporates 53 security features, compared with 23 in the previous version. These include a transparent window, QR code, ultraviolet features, hologram and microtext.
The enhancements were introduced to ensure the identity card's security features remained relevant to technological advancements, following about 12 years of use of the previous MyKad generation.
"JPN has taken steps to further upgrade the security features. That is why we call it the new-generation MyKad," he said.

"Johor recorded the highest number, with 31,392 cards issued, followed by Kuala Lumpur with 29,601, Selangor (26,736), Sarawak (25,642) and Sabah (22,523)," he told a press conference after officiating the 78th National Registration Day celebration and the launch of the MADANI Adopted Village and MADANI Adopted School initiatives at the Kampung Melayu Sedenak Multipurpose Hall here today.
Saifuddin Nasution said the public need not rush to replace their MyKad, as JPN had assured them that the supply of cards was sufficient to meet demand.

He said about 24 million existing MyKad were currently in circulation, while JPN received an average of 200,000 applications a month for various purposes, including new identity cards, replacements for damaged cards and MyKad issuance to those turning 18.

He said possession of a MyKad was becoming increasingly important due to various government initiatives requiring its use, including purchases of petrol and cooking oil, as well as the redemption of Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA).

"We do not have any projections. We will continue as usual and serve the public. What matters is ensuring that the card supply is sufficient to meet demand from those who choose to switch to the new-generation MyKad," he said.
7c3ad78b18a763f6: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The family of Noorizwan Zulkefly, who died earlier this month while under the custody of the Cheras district police, brought their fight for justice directly to the prime minister's doorstep this morning, demanding an independent and transparent inquiry into the circumstances surrounding his death.

Accompanied by legal counsel from rights group Lawyers for Liberty (LFL), the 42-year-old deceased's family arrived at Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's private residence in Bandar Sungai Long, gathering at the entrance before security personnel ushered them into the compound to deliver a formal protest memorandum to the prime minister's representative, NST reported.

The memorandum, handed over by Noorizwan's younger brother Nooranis Zulkefly, expressed profound alarm over unexplained physical injuries documented during the post-mortem examination, urging Putrajaya to intervene directly to prevent an institutional cover-up.

Pathologists at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM) in Cheras confirmed that while the post-mortem detected no structural trauma to internal organs, Noorizwan's body bore multiple external contusions and injuries.

The formal medical cause of death remains uncertified and has been officially recorded as "pending laboratory analysis" while the Chemistry Department conducts specialised toxicological and histopathological tests.
Noorizwan was arrested by Cheras police personnel on Sept 19 under Section 39A(1) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, along with allegations of burglary and theft under the Penal Code.

Following 11 days in police lock-up, his physical condition deteriorated sharply, prompting authorities to transfer him to HCTM on Sept 30, where medical staff pronounced him dead in the early hours of Oct 1.

The family's petition follows public remarks by Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus, who defended the custodial administration by insisting officers followed standard operating procedures to the letter before the detainee took ill.
Fadil had publicly noted that Noorizwan held 44 prior criminal records, mainly related to narcotics and property theft, and had confessed to multiple break-ins in the Cheras district.

Bukit Aman's specialised Criminal Investigation and Deaths in Custody Unit (USJKT) has since expanded its internal affairs investigation, questioning 78 witnesses ranging from police personnel and medical specialists to legal aid representatives and the victim's immediate family.

9297bc4509cdc327: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Josiah Hogan believes all actors should be given equal opportunities to demonstrate their acting abilities, rather than having roles allocated based primarily on popularity.
The 40-year-old actor said that given sufficient room to perform, an actor could deliver a performance that exceeds expectations.

Referring to his own experience of rarely being a production’s first choice, Josiah said he had worked hard to prove his capabilities, as demonstrated by his portrayal of SAC Kamal in the film Takluk 2: Op Daulat.
“I am often the second, third or fourth choice for a role. Even for SAC Kamal, I was the fourth choice, but my scene with Datuk Eman Manan went viral.

“We do not necessarily have to cast actors whose schedules are packed (popular actors). We can also consider those who are available, because an actor who is less busy may be more focused and deliver a much better performance,” he told reporters after the pre-launch of Takluk 2: Op Daulat here recently.
Josiah said a similar situation was common in Hollywood, where actors who were not the first choice had managed to create magic on screen, turning films into major hits.
Actor Josiah Hogan after an interview with Bernama at the pre-launch of ‘Takluk 2: Op Daulat’ at Wisma Pertahanan recently. — Bernama pic

Sharing his views on the craft of acting, he said the key to successfully portraying a character lay in an actor’s ability to understand the character’s mood and demeanour when delivering lines, rather than merely memorising the dialogue.

“As actors, the challenge lies in understanding a character and switching according to the situation. When we focus too much on the dialogue, we sometimes forget the character’s own mannerisms,” he said.

Directed by Zulkarnain Azhar, the film is inspired by the 2013 Lahad Datu incursion and Ops Daulat, during which Malaysian security forces defended the country’s sovereignty. It is a continuation of Takluk: Lahad Datu, which was released in 2024.
Takluk 2: Op Daulat, scheduled to hit cinemas on November 26, also stars Syafiq Kyle, Datuk Remy Ishak, Kamal Adli and Sara Ali. — Bernama
15d6442634660027: PALANGKARAYA (Indonesia), Oct 24 — Hundreds of students protested late Friday in Indonesia’s Palangkaraya, demanding the government do more to tackle a wildfire crisis that has shrouded their city and the wider region in toxic haze for months.

The students, many wearing surgical masks, gathered under an eerily orange sky with severely reduced visibility and waved banners urging authorities to declare a national emergency to free up more aid.

“The officials are morons, yet they get fantastic perks while the lives of the common people are tragic,” read one protest placard nailed to a wall outside the office of the governor of Central Kalimantan — an Indonesian province on the island of Borneo where the fires are taking place.
The demonstrators sang the Indonesia Pusaka patriotic song and engaged in light skirmishes with police.
No injuries or arrests were reported and as night fell, the protesters cleared up their trash before dispersing peacefully.

“We call upon the Central Kalimantan provincial government to state clearly that it is unable to mitigate this disaster, so that the situation may be officially designated a national disaster,” protest leader Yuyun Sanjaya told the crowd.
“How is it possible that such thick, dense smoke is being inhaled by helpless elderly people and newborn infants, and the government simply lets it happen?”
Wildfires have burned more than 1.9 million hectares in the nine months to September, according to deforestation monitor Nusantara Atlas — a figure the government has not confirmed or denied.
The resulting haze has sickened hundreds of thousands in Indonesia and reached as far as Malaysia, Singapore and East Timor.
Amid diplomatic objections from neighbouring countries, patience has also been running thin at home, with sporadic anti-government protests.
On Thursday, Indonesian school children prayed for rain on Java island, where fires have also ravaged several regencies and conservation areas. — AFP

346822a1c7bdd55c: GEORGE TOWN: Bahasa Melayu perlu diperkasakan dalam dunia digital menerusi penghasilan kandungan kreatif dan berilmu bagi menarik minat generasi muda untuk menggunakannya, sekali gus memartabatkan bahasa kebangsaan.

Menteri Pendidikan, Fadhlina Sidek, berkata mereka yang lahir pada 2010 hingga 2024 atau generasi alpha, memperoleh pendedahan bahasa bukan sahaja melalui buku teks dan bilik darjah, malah menerusi video, permainan digital, animasi, muzik, kandungan penstriman dan interaksi dalam talian.

“Saya percaya bahasa Melayu mempunyai masa hadapan yang cerah, sekiranya kita berani mengubah pendekatan dan memperluas ruang penggunaannya. Kita tidak boleh sekadar meminta generasi muda mencintai bahasa Melayu.

“Kita perlu membawa bahasa Melayu ke dalam dunia digital mereka (alpha) melalui kandungan bermutu, animasi kreatif, permainan pendidikan, video pendek yang berilmu, penerbitan elektronik dan aplikasi berasaskan teknologi terkini,” katanya pada Majlis Pelancaran Bulan Bahasa Kebangsaan 2026 Peringkat Kebangsaan di Padang Kota Lama, hari ini.
Teks ucapannya dibacakan Timbalan Ketua Pengarah Pendidikan (Sektor Pembangunan Profesionalisme) Amzan Abd Malek.

Fadhlina berkata, kerajaan turut memberikan penekanan kepada pembangunan teknologi digital dan kecerdasan buatan (AI) dalam Belanjawan Madani 2027, khususnya komitmen kerajaan untuk menggembleng sumber kementerian, agensi dan institusi pendidikan bagi menyumbang data bahasa digital yang sahih dan beranotasi kepada Dewan Bahasa dan Pustaka (DBP).

Beliau berkata, kerjasama Kementerian Pendidikan (KPM) dengan DBP melahirkan 259 Munsyi Remaja menerusi Program Pembinaan Munsyi Remaja, selain membina 1,924 Munsyi Siswa dan 970 Munsyi Muda, di samping peranan lebih 500 orang Munsyi Dewan di seluruh negara.

Menurutnya, KPM melalui DBP turut memperluas pengiktirafan terhadap kecemerlangan dalam bidang penulisan, akademik serta pemartabatan bahasa dan sastera Melayu kepada pelajar institusi pengajian tinggi menerusi Anugerah Bitara DBP mulai tahun ini.

Beliau turut menegaskan kepentingan memelihara tulisan Jawi sebagai khazanah persuratan Melayu yang merakam perkembangan ilmu, pemikiran dan budaya masyarakat, dengan usaha itu perlu digerakkan secara bersama oleh sekolah, ibu bapa, institusi pendidikan dan DBP.

Bagi memperkukuh usaha pemartabatan bahasa kebangsaan, Fadhlina mengumumkan KPM bersetuju menyediakan peruntukan RM10,000 kepada setiap agensi, institusi pengajian tinggi (IPT), Institut Pendidikan Guru (IPG) dan pertubuhan bukan kerajaan (NGO) yang melaksanakan program pemartabatan bahasa kebangsaan pada 2027.

Beliau berkata inisiatif itu bertujuan memperluas penyertaan pelbagai pihak, memperkukuh kerjasama strategik dan menggalakkan pelaksanaan program yang berimpak tinggi sekali gus diharap dapat membina gerakan lebih tersusun dalam usaha memperkukuh penggunaan bahasa kebangsaan di seluruh negara.

Mengenai sambutan Bulan Bahasa Kebangsaan 2026, Fadhlina berkata tema “Bahasa Kita Wajah Kita” mengingatkan bahawa bahasa bukan sekadar alat komunikasi, malah mencerminkan identiti, nilai dan budaya sekali gus menjadi antara asas penting dalam membina persefahaman dan perpaduan dalam masyarakat berbilang kaum dan bahasa ibunda.
Pada majlis tersebut, Bernama Radio menerima Hadiah Citra Sahabat DBP 2026 sebagai pengiktirafan atas sumbangan dan komitemen dalam usaha memperkasakan bahasa Melayu.
